change money verb

also exchange money, exchange, currency exchange, exchange currency

classical

M-O
Plin. NH 33.45: placuitque dēnārium XVI assibus permūtārī
Cic. Att. 12.24.1 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 311

permūtāre

exchange money, coin for coin or one currency for another

In business Latin, to exchange money, and to send it abroad by a bill of exchange (Cic. Att. 12.24.1; Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • permūtātiō, permūtātiōnis f. — an exchange of money; payment by a bill of exchange

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 3.5.4: quae mihi ex pūblicā permūtātiōne dēbētur, (the money) due to me from the public exchange

Examples

  • placuitque dēnārium XVI assibus permūtārī, quīnārium octōnīs, sēstertium quaternīs

    and it was decided that a denarius should be exchanged for sixteen asses, a quinarius for eight and a sesterce for fourPlin. NH 33.45

See also money-changer, currency, change, rate, trade.

SourcesLewis & Short: permuto · Lewis & Short: permutatio
